title: Attended family discharge planning meetings and 30-day readmission in adults aged 75 and over: a case-control study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between an attended family discharge meeting with a written plan and unplanned readmission within 30 days in adults aged 75 and over. Design: case-control study of 160 readmitted cases and 320 frequency-matched controls discharged from medical wards in 2023 to 2025, with exposure read from social work notes. Analysis: logistic regression adjusted for six measures of case complexity. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Family involvement in discharge planning reduced readmission in trials, but routine meetings are chosen for complex patients, which makes crude comparisons misleading. The hospital is considering making meetings standard for patients over 75.
methods: Cases are unplanned readmissions within 30 days; controls are frequency matched by discharge quarter and ward group. Two senior social workers read notes with a fixed abstraction form, blind to case status where possible, with 10 percent read twice. Complexity is measured from discharge summaries. The analysis plan and covariates were fixed before reading.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present sampling, reader agreement, the exposure distribution, crude and adjusted odds ratios, and the three-level exposure analysis.
discussion: The discussion will weigh the estimate against the retrieved trials and matched comparison, examine residual confounding by family engagement, and state what the result means for making meetings standard.
limitations: Residual confounding; readmissions elsewhere missed; exposure read from notes of variable quality.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will be limited to the association in this hospital and will not claim that meetings prevent readmission.
summary: STROBE-structured draft with results left empty until analysis.
